rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The law of conservation of linear momentum states that the total momentum of an isolated system remains constant. It is a powerful tool for solving collision, explosion, and recoil problems. While momentum is conserved in all collisions, kinetic energy is only conserved in perfectly elastic ones.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Conservation: $\sum \vec{p}_i = \sum \vec{p}_f$
1D Collision: $m_1 u_1 + m_2 u_2 = m_1 v_1 + m_2 v_2$
Perfectly Inelastic: $m_1 u_1 + m_2 u_2 = (m_1 + m_2) v$

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Isolated System Requirement:** Momentum conservation ($\sum \vec{p}_i = \sum \vec{p}_f$) holds strictly only when the net *external* force on the system is zero. External forces like gravity, friction, or applied pushes must be absent or balanced.  ·  **Collisions vs. Continuous Interaction:** In a collision, the interaction is brief and impulsive; internal forces dominate. In continuous interactions (e.g., rocket propulsion), momentum is conserved at each instant, but mass changes must be tracked using the variable-mass form $F = dp/dt$.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Note 1: Always define the system clearly.  ·  Note 2: Use vector notation for 2D problems.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Example 1 (1D collision): $m_1 u_1 + m_2 u_2 = (m_1 + m_2) v$ for perfectly inelastic.  ·  Example 2 (Explosion): A shell at rest breaks into two pieces $m_1, m_2$ with velocities $v_1, v_2$ such that $m_1 v_1 + m_2 v_2 = 0$.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: ❌ 'Momentum is conserved only in elastic collisions.' ✅ Momentum is conserved in ALL collisions (elastic or inelastic) as long as the system is isolated.  ·  ❌ 'Kinetic energy is always conserved in collisions.' ✅ Only in perfectly elastic collisions. In inelastic collisions, KE is lost.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Added new rich content for important Concepts.  ·  The law of conservation of linear momentum: Σp = constant when ΣF_ext = 0 — one of the most fundamental laws in physics.  ·  Newton's third law implies momentum conservation: action-reaction pairs produce equal and opposite momentum changes.  ·  Recoil: a special case where a system initially at rest separates into parts with equal and opposite momenta.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Isolated system = no external force.  ·  Momentum is always conserved in collisions.  ·  Kinetic energy is conserved ONLY in elastic collisions.  ·  Recoil and explosions are momentum conservation problems.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The law of conservation of momentum is one of the fundamental laws of physics, derived from the homogeneity of space (Noether's theorem).  ·  It holds true from subatomic particle collisions in accelerators to the motion of galaxies.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: **Law of Conservation of Linear Momentum:** In an isolated system (no external net force), the total linear momentum remains constant: $\sum \vec{p}_i = \sum \vec{p}_f$. This is a fundamental law derived from the homogeneity of space (Noether's theorem). It is a direct consequence of the fact that the laws of physics are the same at all points in space.  ·  **Isolated System:** A system where the net external force is zero. Internal forces (like collision forces) do not change the total momentum because they act in equal and opposite pairs (Newton's 3rd law). The system can be as small as two colliding particles or as large as the entire universe.  ·  **Coefficient of Restitution (e):** A measure of elasticity in collisions: $e = (v_2 - v_1) / (u_1 - u_2)$. $e=1$ (perfectly elastic), $0 < e < 1$ (inelastic), $e=0$ (perfectly inelastic). This coefficient depends on the materials of the colliding objects and their surface properties.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Rocket propulsion: continuous ejection of mass produces continuous thrust — the variable-mass momentum problem.  ·  Momentum conservation applies component-wise: a direction with zero net external force conserves momentum along that direction regardless of other directions.  ·  Application formula for Conservation of Linear Momentum

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Derivation result for Conservation of Linear Momentum  ·  **Kinetic Energy Distinction:** Momentum is conserved in *all* isolated collisions (elastic or inelastic). Kinetic energy is conserved *only* in perfectly elastic collisions. In inelastic collisions, some KE is converted to heat, sound, or deformation energy.  ·  ❌ 'Internal forces change the total momentum.' ✅ Internal forces (like collision forces) cancel out in pairs (Newton's 3rd law) and do not change the total momentum of the system.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ 'Conservation of momentum applies to individual objects.' ✅ It applies to the SYSTEM of objects.  ·  Carefully distinguish between similar-looking concepts in conservation of linear momentum.  ·  Pay attention to the conditions under which formulas and theorems apply.
